clue.text: Dog found mostly to point out game

indicators.note: mostly means the word is used without its last letter, so most but not all of it survives

parts.note: to found a company is to base it, establish it
a setter dog sets, standing still to show the hunter where game lies

explanation.surface: A hunting dog is discovered, mostly, indicating where the quarry is hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims BASE to BAS. 'Point out game' is not a game being pointed out: it is what a gun dog does when it sets.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged hound bred for hunting by scent.

clue.text: Incredible start to argument, then we part

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
some means a part, a portion

explanation.surface: An argument opens remarkably, and then we separate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' looks like a verb (we split up) but it is the noun, some.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome in its modern sense means amazing or wonderful.

clue.text: (Combat)ant?

parts.note: the whole word is a fighter; the bracketed part set aside leaves an insect of a fighting caste

explanation.surface: A bracketed word puzzle about a fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the whole word as a fighting man, and the unbracketed 'ant' as the insect caste that defends the nest.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter in an army, and also the large-jawed defending caste in an ant colony.

clue.text: Car deal?.Hurry up to get one from Germany

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to dart is to hurry
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: Rushing to buy a German-made car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses DART to TRAD in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old car handed over in part payment for a new one.

clue.text: This policeman can't stop you at any rate

definitions.text: This policeman can't stop you at any rate

parts.words: This policeman can't stop you at any rate
parts.note: read 'at any rate' literally: this officer's job is stopping motorists who go too fast

explanation.surface: A policeman who seems powerless to halt anyone at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At any rate' sounds like 'in any case', but it is literal: this officer stops you only at excessive rates of speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic officer who enforces speed limits on motorists.

clue.text: Feeble sound is evident in erotic entertainment

parts.note: a peep is a faint little sound
something that shows is visible, evident

explanation.surface: A faint noise is audible during a racy show.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'peep-shows' stands for the category of entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Peep-shows are booths where viewers pay to watch titillating displays.

clue.text: Enter rocks after huge earthquake's beginning

indicators.note: after puts the shaken word behind the huge one

parts.note: something epic is huge, on a grand scale

indicators.note: rocks means shakes about, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Get in as the ground shakes once a massive quake starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' rearranges ENTER to ENTRE. 'earthquake' feeds the surface of shaking, but 'earthquake's beginning' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the point on the surface above the origin of a seismic shock.

clue.text: Central heating repeatedly moving air without very loud racket

parts.note: CH is the estate agents' abbreviation for central heating

indicators.note: without means outside, so the doubled letters go round the very
repeatedly means the moved word is used twice
moving means the letters are shifted round

explanation.surface: A heating system keeps shifting air outside, making a din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking; the doubled scrambled pair goes round V. CH is the usual property-advert shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a cacophony, originally mock serenading with pots and pans.

clue.text: Old-fashioned enjoyment in a new church after prayers

indicators.note: after puts the prayers in front of the rest

parts.note: pleas are earnest requests or prayers
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Delight felt in a new church once prayers are said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here; nothing is inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasance is an archaic word for pleasure or delight.

clue.text: Ruthless man suppressing cry of pain

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down, so the cry is taken out of the man and silenced

parts.note: a fellow is a man, a chap
ow is what you say when hurt

explanation.surface: A cruel man stifles a yelp of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell is an old literary adjective meaning cruel or deadly, as in 'one fell swoop'.

clue.text: Wanting public reputation, prolonged sensation

parts.note: to be after something is to want it
a public figure's image is how others see them

explanation.surface: Someone craving public standing finds the feeling lingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' looks like 'lacking', but here it means desiring, as in being after something.
explanation.definitionFit: An afterimage is a visual impression that persists after the stimulus has gone.

clue.text: Reduction in staff attached to reserve force

indicators.note: a reduction in the word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: a staff is a pole or rod
reserve as cool aloofness of manner is ice

explanation.surface: Cutting staff numbers linked to the reserve army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees; it is a pole, shortened to POL. 'Reserve' is not a military reserve but an icy manner.
explanation.definitionFit: The police are often called 'the force', a body of law officers.

clue.text: They avoid pleasure or access it differently

indicators.note: taking the letters differently means arranging them in a new order

explanation.surface: Some people shun enjoyment, or else reach it by another route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges ACCESS IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascetics are self-denying people who renounce comforts and indulgence.

clue.text: German operas suffice for chivalrous deeds

parts.note: der is the German word for 'the'
Wagner's Ring cycle is a set of four operas
to do is to suffice, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: Some German operas are enough to stand in for knightly exploits.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's Der Ring des Nibelungen gives RING for 'operas'.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is heroic, daring action, the stuff of chivalric romance.

clue.text: There's a place in the worship of God for indomitable rule

indicators.note: in puts the place inside the worship of God

parts.note: deism is belief in God based on reason
a spot is a place

explanation.surface: Worshipping God leaves room for absolute authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' is a link; DE + SPOT + ISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Despotism is tyrannical rule that brooks no opposition.

clue.text: Reviving rent cut, followed later by steep hike

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an ascent is a climb up a slope

explanation.surface: A rent reduction is followed by a sharp increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hike' suggests a price rise to suit the rent, but it is a climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn, coming back to life.

clue.text: Wrought iron isn't used around English enclosure

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the English
wrought means worked, so the letters are hammered into a new form

explanation.surface: Wrought iron is not used around English fencing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrought' looks like part of the phrase 'wrought iron', but it is the anagram signal; 'around' then wraps the result round E.
explanation.definitionFit: An insertion is something put in, an enclosure in a letter.

clue.text: German school exercises take place here

definitions.meaning: a German secondary school preparing students for university
a gym hall where people work out

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a German grammar school and a hall for physical training.

clue.text: A writer or two

definitions.meaning: Mark ..., the American author of Tom Sawyer
... is an old word for a pair, as in 'never the ... shall meet'

explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain is a famous pen name, and twain is archaic for the number following one.

clue.text: Paper is pushed back into cavity

indicators.note: pushed back means the paper and the is are written in reverse order as one run

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper is shoved into a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pushed back' turns the whole run of paper plus is; 'into' is a link, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is a hollow in the bone of the skull, an air-filled space.

clue.text: Stand up after French man and woman's entrance

indicators.note: after puts the standing up behind the man and woman

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, the French title for a man
Esme is a woman's name
to rise is to get to one's feet

explanation.surface: Getting to one's feet once a French couple make their entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like a noun (a way in) but it is the verb, stressed on the second syllable; ''s' is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to hold them spellbound, to hypnotise or enthral them.

clue.text: Inaccurately try and fail to catch?

parts.note: the prefix mis means wrongly or inaccurately
a judge tries or hears a case

explanation.surface: Someone tries clumsily and fails to grab hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' means hear, as a court tries a case; 'catch' is catching words.
explanation.definitionFit: To mishear is to not make out correctly what was said.

clue.text: Hard shot to secure round? Attempt to lift poor driver

indicators.note: to secure means to hold the round inside
shot means ruined or knocked about, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: in a down clue, to lift a word is to raise it, reading it backwards

parts.note: a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: A golfer's hard shot to save the round, and a try to get the ball up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' scrambles, 'to secure' holds O inside, and 'to lift' turns the attempt upward. Golf words in the surface hide a selfish motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hog is a reckless or inconsiderate motorist.

clue.text: Site, having removed one nettle, may be barren

indicators.note: having removed means one letter is taken out of the site

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to nettle is to annoy, to rile

explanation.surface: A plot cleared of a nettle may be infertile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nettle' looks like a plant but is the verb, irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile land is unproductive, unable to support growth.

clue.text: Operating overflow?

parts.note: split the second word as over plus flow: over is on, flow is a stream, and the whole means working

explanation.surface: A working spillage from a tank.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'overflow' as two words: 'over' is a sense of the first word and 'flow' a sense of the second, while 'Operating' defines the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant or a process that is up and running, in production.

clue.text: Some fields have never cropped

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some fields have never had their crop harvested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks out a run from 'fields have never'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair that is shorn close has been cut short, cropped.

clue.text: Nasty big lie repeated about Newton is unjustified

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
nasty suggests something messed about, so the letters are scrambled
repeated means the word lie appears twice in the fodder

parts.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: A vile whopper told twice about Isaac Newton is unwarranted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' doubles the lie before 'Nasty' scrambles everything; 'about' then puts Newton's symbol inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineligible means not qualified or entitled, so a claim with no warrant.

clue.text: Hard look that might come as a shock

definitions.text: that might come as a shock

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an air is a look or manner, as in 'an air of mystery'

explanation.surface: A stern glance that could give someone a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests a fright; it is a thick mass, a shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a bushy, unruly mass on the head.

clue.text: Cry of surprise about school's figure of speech

indicators.note: about means the cry wraps round the school, which sits inside it

parts.note: 'My, my!' is an exclamation of surprise
Eton is the English public school

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in astonishment at a school's turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The cry is the doubled 'My, my!', which goes round ETON after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Metonymy is a rhetorical figure naming a thing by something associated with it, like 'the Crown' for the monarch.

clue.text: In tears, being teased

definitions.meaning: in tatters, torn, with rips in it
teased or tormented, as students rag one another

explanation.definitionFit: Ragged means torn and tattered, and ragged is also the past participle of rag, to tease.
